raw_segments.text: At first she would have nothing to do with his wicked scheme,
for she was of a good natural disposition.
Thirty more over there was a bard with her,
to whom Agamemnon had given strict orders on setting out for Troy,
that he was to keep guard over his wife.
But when heaven had counseled her destruction,
Agisthus carried this bard off to a desert island
and left him there for crows and seagulls to batten upon,
after which she went willingly enough to the house of Agisthus.
Then he offered many burnt sacrifices to the gods,
and decorated many temples with tapestries and gilding,
for he had succeeded far beyond his expectations.
